name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
summary: An isolation exercise using a high cable pulley and bar attachment to target the triceps through elbow extension.

setup: Attach a straight or angled bar to a high cable pulley.
Grasp the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, roughly shoulder-width or slightly narrower.
Step close to the cable, hinge forward slightly at the hips, brace your core, and pin your upper arms tight to your ribs.
steps: Begin with your elbows fully flexed at roughly chest height while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Push the bar straight down by extending your elbows until your arms are fully locked out.
Squeeze your triceps firmly at the bottom of the movement.
Control the bar back up to the starting position under tension, allowing full elbow flexion without letting your upper arms drift forward.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you push the bar down into full extension, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
cues: Glue your elbows to your sides
Snap the arms straight at the bottom
Control the weight on the way up

common_faults.fault: Flaring or drifting the elbows forward and backward during repetitions.
common_faults.correction: Lock your upper arms against your torso and move strictly at the elbow joint.

common_faults.fault: Using torso momentum or leaning heavily over the bar to press the weight down.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the load and maintain a steady, slightly hinged torso posture throughout the set.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the range of motion short at the top or bottom.
common_faults.correction: Allow full flexion at the top for a deep stretch and reach complete extension at the bottom.

precautions: Ensure the attachment carabiner is fully locked before loading the cable.
